title: Inhaled Treprostinil for Idiopathic Pulmonary Fibrosis
Whole-exome sequencing reveals novel and previously reported variants in genes linked to white matter pathology in neurodevelopmental disorders
abstract: Abstract Functional neuronal networks are essential for brain growth and development, with myelin or “white matter” playing a key role not just in neuronal transmission but also in axonal support, maintenance, and repair. Disruption of these networks through genetic variation contributes to a range of neurodevelopmental disorders, including both primary inherited white matter disorders and an ever increasing list of secondary leukodystrophies or leucoencephalopathies. Traditionally identified using neuroimaging techniques such as magnetic resonance imaging (MRI), clinico-radiological heterogeneity means MRI alone is rarely sufficient in providing a diagnosis requiring integration with genomic techniques and expert medical review. In this study, we describe an exome-first approach in a cohort of 78 consanguineous families with undiagnosed neurodevelopmental disorders in a healthcare resource-poor setting. The aim is to demonstrate that, even in the absence of MRI imaging, we have the potential to improve diagnostic accuracy and yield. We report positive findings in six families, including known variants in MLC1, AIMP1, ASPA, and DEGS1 , and novel variants in XPA and POLR3B . This study highlights the effectiveness of whole-exome sequencing as a diagnostic tool for heterogeneous neurological disorders and provides additional evidence supporting gene-disease associations in conditions linked to white matter pathology.

title: Wellbeing While Waiting: Effectiveness and implementation of youth social prescribing for young people awaiting CAMHS support
abstract: Abstract Prolonged waiting times for Child and Adolescent Mental Health Services (CAMHS) leave many young people without structured support while awaiting specialist treatment. Social prescribing has been proposed as a community-based adjunct within CAMHS pathways; however, evidence regarding its safety and clinical impact remains limited. Wellbeing While Waiting was a multi-site non-randomised controlled trial embedded within a hybrid type II implementation–effectiveness evaluation conducted across 11 CAMHS in England. The protocol was prospectively published prior to recruitment (BMC Psychiatry; https://doi.org/10.1186/s12888-023-04758-0 ). Between May 2023 and March 2025, 558 young people aged 11–18 years referred to CAMHS were enrolled (225 usual care; 333 social prescribing). Primary outcomes were anxiety and depression symptoms, total emotional and behavioural difficulties, and perceived stress. Secondary outcomes included resilience and wellbeing. No intervention-related adverse events were observed. On average, participants had 5 sessions with a Link Worker. Compared with usual care, no significant differences were observed in anxiety or depression symptoms. However, participants receiving social prescribing demonstrated significant improvements in total emotional and behavioural difficulties over six months, driven by reductions in conduct difficulties, hyperactivity and peer problems. Significant improvements for those receiving social prescribing were also found for prosocial behaviour and resilience. Within routine CAMHS pathways, no intervention-related adverse events were observed for social prescribing, and social prescribing was associated with improvements in behavioural and resilience-related outcomes, although not in anxiety or depressive symptoms. Findings suggest social prescribing may offer a valuable adjunct during delayed access to specialist treatment, with effects distinct from symptom-focused clinical therapies.

title: Unveiling the determinants of shareholder activism in listed firms: empirical evidence from India
abstract: Purpose This study investigates the determinants of shareholder activism (SA) in the Indian context. This investigation aims to identify factors that significantly contribute to the likelihood of SA in a developing country setting, such as India, to provide meaningful insights into the determinants and dimensions of SA. Design/methodology/approach This study uses content analysis and a binary panel logit model to investigate the relationship between various explanatory variables and the likelihood of SA. Content analysis was used to identify the determinants of SA and categorise them into various types of demands, based on existing literature. Furthermore, a binary panel logit model is used to assess the significance of the independent variables and their classification accuracy, using a sample of 46 listed Indian firms where SA occurred. Findings The findings suggest that the determinants of SA in India are multifaceted. SA has gained momentum in recent years, with governance-related demands being the primary issue. The panel logit model suggests that major governance-related, financial restructuring–related, related party transactions–related and remuneration-related factors significantly affected the likelihood of SA. Research limitations/implications This study provides valuable insights into the determinants of SA, thereby contributing to the limited existing literature in this domain. These findings will also highlight the need to study SA in the Indian context and can act as a foundation for further exploration. Practical implications This study’s findings will inform policymakers on the governance reforms needed to integrate SA as a tool for safeguarding minority shareholders’ interests. Originality/value This study’s originality lies in the fact that very little literature is available in the Indian context, and SA has evolved significantly over the past years. This study will help highlight the importance and utility of SA in the Indian context.

title: Trends and research frontiers in post-disaster housing: a bibliometric analysis
journal: International Journal of Disaster Resilience in the Built Environment
abstract: Purpose This study aims to examine trends and annual publications in post-disaster housing research, identify influential journals, authors and countries and explore geospatial contributions, frequently cited papers and co-occurring keywords in the field. Design/methodology/approach This study provides a comprehensive exploration of the post-disaster housing research field through a bibliometric analysis and scientometric analysis of 276 publications published between 2007 and 2024, sourced from the Scopus database. Findings The study highlights current trends and influential journals in post-disaster housing research. Gonzalo Lizarralde from Université de Montréal is the most prolific author, while the USA, Australia and the UK are the most active contributors. The most cited study in this domain is Davidson et al. (2007). Key recurring keywords include “post-disaster housing and reconstruction”, “recovery and resilience” and “temporary and transitional housing”. Research limitations/implications The analysis is limited to Scopus-indexed publications, potentially excluding relevant studies from other sources. Findings suggest that incorporating resilience and participatory design theories can address immediate and long-term housing needs post-disaster, considering economic, environmental, social and cultural factors. Originality/value To the best of the authors’ knowledge, this study presents the first bibliometric analysis of prior research on post-disaster housing. It significantly advances the existing body of knowledge in the post-disaster housing research domain. Notably, the study highlights a gap in the literature regarding the “cultural and contextual adaptation”, “technological innovations in reconstruction” and “economic viability and affordability” aspects of post-disaster housing, emphasising the need for further exploration in this area. This study focuses on housing responses to natural hazards such as floods, hurricanes, earthquakes and landslides, excluding conflict-induced displacement.

title: Towards the pedagogical validation of science CEFR-aligned literacy descriptors in secondary CLIL classroom interaction: insights from physics teaching episodes
abstract: Abstract This study aims to pedagogically validate CEFR-aligned science descriptors, in particular, contributing towards physics literacy descriptors. It explores how disciplinary literacies align with the pedagogical talk and actions of a CLIL Physics teacher, drawing on Dalton-Puffer’s construct of Cognitive Discourse Functions (CDFs). CDFs have proven useful for identifying subject-specific language demands in L2 content subjects and serve as the foundation for a heuristic assessment tool for CEFR-disciplinary literacy descriptors. Using classroom interaction data, the study examines the applicability of CEFR-aligned disciplinary literacy descriptors – originally developed for assessing students’ writing – to teacher talk in whole-class teaching episodes. The study pursues two aims: first, to provide qualitative insights into how the CDFs Define, Describe and Explain are embedded in pedagogical meaning-making in a seventh-grade bilingual CLIL Physics lesson, using two complementary analytical approaches; and second, to explore how these insights can inform and refine the heuristic tool for CEFR-aligned science literacy descriptors. The findings contribute to the pedagogical validation and further development of the heuristic assessment tool, strengthening its relevance and applicability for classroom interaction in secondary CLIL Physics education.

title: The paradoxical salesperson – an attempt to gauge multidexterity
abstract: Purpose This study aims to examine personal selling through a paradox lens to explore the inherent dualities that salespeople navigate in their day-to-day roles. Design/methodology/approach Adopting a qualitative research design and grounded in the theories-in-use approach. The empirical evidence is based on 21 in-depth interviews conducted using theoretical sampling procedures. Findings This study identifies three forms of paradoxes: paradox of belongingness, paradox of learning and paradox of performance that salespeople deal with. Notably, each of these paradoxes entails inherent tensions. Research limitations/implications This study has three key limitations. First, it is confined to exploring dualities and paradoxes within the domain of personal selling and sales management, thereby limiting its scope to a specific functional context. Second, the exclusive reliance on a qualitative research design restricts the generalizability of the findings and does not provide objective, quantifiable evidence. Third, the study identifies only three forms of paradoxes, leaving the paradox of organizing unexamined within the present investigation. Originality/value To the best of the author’s knowledge, this is the first study of its kind that has aimed to see personal selling through paradoxical lens and present personal selling as a multidextrous activity.

title: Steering networked ambidexterity under institutional voids: evidence from Iranian biotechnology SMEs
abstract: Purpose Research on networked ambidexterity still tends to separate structural accounts of alliance networks from micro-foundational accounts of managerial action. This study examines how managers in Iranian biotechnology SMEs sustain exploration and exploitation under institutional voids and how these practices support productive entrepreneurship in a resource-constrained setting. Design/methodology/approach A qualitative grounded theory design was used. Eighteen in-depth interviews were conducted with senior managers from biotechnology SMEs in Iran, and the material was analyzed iteratively through open, axial and selective coding following Strauss's procedures. Findings The analysis identifies the core managerial role of the “paradoxical bridge,” through which managers translate between scientific exploration and commercial exploitation. Four steering mechanisms support this role: relational/power governance, pragmatic knowledge governance, situational conflict resolution and proactive network reconfiguration. These mechanisms culminate in six contingent archetypal configurations that sustain ambidexterity and productive entrepreneurship in different ways under institutional constraints. Practical implications The findings highlight the importance of the bridging role, deliberate network design and context-sensitive steering routines for managers in constrained innovation ecosystems. For policymakers, the study points to the value of strengthening intermediary support, regulatory transparency and coordination mechanisms that enable productive entrepreneurship. Originality/value The study offers an empirically grounded mechanism-based account of networked ambidexterity in an emerging-economy setting. It shows how cognition is enacted through relational practice, clarifies how institutional voids shape managerial steering and develops a contingent configurational framework rather than a universal model of ambidexterity.
